findings.issue: save() replaces the durable registry before validating it. Repeating an otherwise valid create-child grant persists duplicate identities, then throws DUPLICATE_IDENTITY and leaves every subsequent load broken. Validate the temporary candidate before publishing it.

The generated local result test checks only truthy principal/execution IDs, and the replay checks only the exact execution ID. A committed result attributed to the wrong principal still passes while its sidecar claims the requested principal. Check the exact pair in the emitted Node test.

The notBeforeMs constraint order emits JSON Schema minimum -9007199254740991 although the runtime rejects negative values. Reorder the constraints and regenerate the current schema without rewriting frozen historical evidence.

The original design still describes expanding writer identity and a revocable lease without identifying it as superseded or linking the final attribution-only sidecar design. Mark the draft as historical and link the canonical study.

needs-human: Original acceptance #7 names revoked credential leases, but the fixture models principal revocation and lease expiry only. Decide whether principal-wide invalidation satisfies the bounded research requirement or whether independent lease revocation needs an explicit contract and probe; do not silently introduce new semantics.

summary: Fixed four defects in registry publication, exact result attribution, generated schema constraints, and superseded documentation; six regression checks pass after five failed before the fixes. Build/typecheck pass, while the pre-existing full suite remains red: 1968 passed and 9 failed across three unchanged test files. needs-human: independent lease-revocation acceptance remains ambiguous, and corrected instruments lack a fresh full Linux/Node 22 replay.
